task_title: Declare a table over HTTP and publish declaration adoption on /metrics
task_criteria: POST /api/ns/:ns/tables/:table/declare writes a declaration through the SAME core as the CLI verb and the MCP tool (declareTable in src/tables/declare.ts), returning the resulting declaration, and an unauthenticated/grant-restricted caller cannot use it (namespace + per-table write grant).
An end-to-end run on a scratch daemon proves an HTTP client can declare a table and immediately insert and read a row, with a pre-fix control (origin/main tree) answering 404 for the same request.

Declaration adoption is a number on the scrape surface: duckbrain_table_declaration_namespaces{format=schema.json|legacy} and duckbrain_table_declarations{format} are sampled from the namespaces root at collect time, emit NO sample when there is no store, and move when a namespace adopts schema.json.

The legacy-vs-schema.json shape decision is recorded in docs (why a partial migration is worse than none, what legacy costs, the per-table recipe with rollback), and the docs name the one path a user should take.
The full suite is green and test-counts.json is bumped in the same commit.

tier2.summary:
INCOMPLETE
  ✓ POST /api/ns/:ns/tables/:table/declare writes a declaration through the SAME core as the CLI verb and the MCP tool (declareTable in src/tables/declare.ts), returning the resulting declaration, and an unauthenticated/grant-restricted caller cannot use it (namespace + per-table write grant).: src/http/routes/tables.ts registers router.post("/:table/declare", requireNamespaceGrant((req)=>param(req,"ns")), requireTableGrant(grantNs, grantTable, "write"), ...) and calls declareTable(spec) imported from src/tables/declare.ts — the same core the CLI (src/cli/tables.ts) and MCP tables_declare use; response body carries {namespace, table, path, format, replacedExisting, declaration} with 201/200. Tests: `npx vitest run src/http/routes/tables-declare-adopt001.test.ts` → "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 5 passed (5)", including line 273-302 "403s a table-restricted token that holds no grant for the NEW table" asserting status 403 and error containing "no write grant for table 'new_table'", plus a namespace-grant 403 case. [resolution 0.14; src/tables/declare.ts]
  ✗ An end-to-end run on a scratch daemon proves an HTTP client can declare a table and immediately insert and read a row, with a pre-fix control (origin/main tree) answering 404 for the same request.: Only half exists. src/http/routes/tables-declare-adopt001.test.ts:134-181 proves declare(201)→insert(201)→read(200), but over an in-process express app (createApp() mounting createTableRoutes on a tmp namespaces root), NOT a scratch daemon boot. The required pre-fix control is entirely absent: grep for "404" in both new test files returns nothing; no e2e script exists (ls scripts/ | grep -i 'e2e|declare|adopt' → empty); no transcript in docs/; the worktree /home/kara/proj-wt-adopt-declared-001 sits at the POST-fix commit d0264bd4, not origin/main; board events for ADOPT-DECLARED-001 contain only task_created and in_progress, no worker summary. The pre-fix tree genuinely lacks the route (git show d0264bd4^:src/http/routes/tables.ts has no /declare route — all 'declare' matches are prose about declared tables), so a 404 control would pass, but it was never executed or recorded.
  ✓ Declaration adoption is a number on the scrape surface: duckbrain_table_declaration_namespaces{format=schema.json|legacy} and duckbrain_table_declarations{format} are sampled from the namespaces root at collect time, emit NO sample when there is no store, and move when a namespace adopts schema.json.: src/http/metrics.ts:643-712: declarationSampler is null when storagePath is absent; publishDeclarations() is wired as `collect:` on both Gauges (collect-time, no timer) and calls withdraw() — declarationNamespaces.remove({format}) / declarationTables.remove({format}) for both formats — when the sampler is null or the census is null, so no sample is emitted. src/metrics/declarations.ts measures schema.json vs tables/<t>.table.json under the namespaces root. Tests: `npx vitest run src/metrics/declarations-adopt001.test.ts` → "Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 8 passed (8)", including line 216 "follows the store: a namespace that adopts schema.json moves the number" (schema.json 0→1 after writeSchema) and line 247 "emits no adoption series for an embedder that declared no store" asserting no /^duckbrain_table_declaration_namespaces\{/m and no /^duckbrain_table_declarations\{/m. [resolution 0.14; schema.json]
  ✓ The legacy-vs-schema.json shape decision is recorded in docs (why a partial migration is worse than none, what legacy costs, the per-table recipe with rollback), and the docs name the one path a user should take.: docs/decisions/ADOPT-DECLARED-001-declaration-shape.md contains all four elements: "Why a partial migration is worse than none" (lines 40-50: legacy always wins on name conflict per src/schema/table-registry.ts, so a schema.json entry beside a legacy file is dead weight that makes a namespace look migrated); "What the legacy shape costs (sourced)" table (lines 52-62, five sourced costs incl. no DB-SUPA-5 change record, no SUPA-2 barrier, no relations/composite keys); "Migration recipe (DECLARE-MIGRATE-001)" per-table 5-step recipe (lines 64-85) with step 5 "Rollback at any point: restore the deleted legacy file — legacy wins again". The one path is named: docs/api/http-api.md:1061 "**Recommended path for a new table: declare it over HTTP (or MCP) without `legacy`**", echoed at docs/guide/cli-reference.md:636. [resolution 0.14; legacy-vs-schema.json]
  ✓ The full suite is green and test-counts.json is bumped in the same commit.: Ran the configured test command `npx vitest run` fresh (log /tmp/vitest_full3.log): "Test Files  268 passed (268)" and "Tests  2261 passed (2261)", Duration 75.67s, no failures. test-counts.json now reads {"suites": 268, "tests": 2261} — exactly matching the live run — and `git show --stat d0264bd4` lists test-counts.json (266→268 suites, 2248→2261 tests) in the SAME commit as the feature. [resolution 0.14; test-counts.json]
The HTTP declare route, metrics gauges, decision docs and green suite (268 files / 2261 tests, counts bumped in-commit) are all real and verified, but criterion 2 is unmet: no scratch-daemon end-to-end run and no pre-fix origin/main 404 control was ever executed or recorded — only an in-process express test.
